title: Decomposing GPTQ execution variability and evaluation-sampling uncertainty

primary.moe: 15 paired columns D = L_FC - L_FR (per-window mean NLL), 3 seeds x 5 groupings; within-seed block centering P_within = diag(P5,P5,P5), df = 12
primary.dense4: 5 grouping columns L_g (G20261111..15); P5, df = 4; ORIGINAL = reference for contrasts only

secondary.dose_natural: k = 1/4/16/64 analysed separately; 8 replicate columns; P8, df = 7; contrasts vs k = 0

exploratory.dose_fixed: fixed act-order dose arrays, same treatment
exploratory.disattenuated_cross_correlation: only if both datasets' corrected-variance CI lower bound > 0

estimand: between-variant variance of dataset-average mean NLL (finite set of executed variants), corrected for evaluation-text sampling: V_corr = V_obs - tr(P Sigma)/df, Sigma = joint bootstrap covariance of the variant mean-NLL vector with identical resampled indices for all variants

resampling.C4HO: window = document (verified one window per distinct document); iid bootstrap of 128 units
resampling.WT2_primary: article cluster bootstrap (window -> majority WikiText-2 test article)
resampling.cluster_estimator: ratio estimator: sum of resampled unit sums / resampled window count

bootstrap.variance_ci: nested bootstrap: Sigma re-estimated in every outer draw; pivot interval for V_corr: [V_corr - q975(V_corr* - V_obs), V_corr - q025(V_corr* - V_obs)] (V_obs = bootstrap-world true finite-set variance); V_obs and V_samp reported with percentile intervals
bootstrap.null_test: common-effect null: remove the centred variant effects from every unit sum (keeps the window-level joint covariance), rerun the nested bootstrap; p = P(V_corr*_null >= V_corr)
bootstrap.sampling_fraction: V_samp / V_obs; interval = 1 - (V_corr pivot interval) / V_obs

split_half.WT2_primary: balanced random article split (shuffle articles, assign to the half with fewer windows)
WT2_sensitivity: chronological first 64 vs last 64 (single deterministic split, confounded by topic/position)
statistics: Pearson of centred effects (MoE: within-seed centred, 15-dim) [primary]
top / bottom agreement (MoE: per seed, averaged)
sign agreement of prespecified non-null contrasts
sign agreement restricted to contrasts with |full-data estimate| > 1 x its own primary-scheme bootstrap SE (rule fixed before results; unthresholded = primary)

contrasts.dense: g - ORIGINAL, 4 non-null groupings (G20261115 = ORIGINAL excluded)

split_half.summary: median, mean, 5th/95th percentiles, frac > 0, frac > 0.5, frac < 0 over partitions; partitions reuse the same windows and are NOT independent replicates

split_half_null.construction: common-effect world (variant effects removed from unit sums); draw a bootstrap dataset of units (same scheme), split its DRAWS with the same balanced rule (each draw is a unit, so the halves are independent iid samples from the effect-free population, as complementary halves of an iid sample are), compute reliability; statistic compared = median Pearson over partitions; p = P(null median >= observed median)

statistics: Pearson / Spearman of full-data centred effects
cross_dataset.ci: independent primary-scheme bootstraps of the two datasets, percentile
cross_dataset.comparability: split-half medians are stepped up to full length with Spearman-Brown 2r/(1+r) before comparison with the full-vs-full cross correlation; expected cross correlation under identical true effects = sqrt(lam_WT2 lam_C4), lam = V_corr / V_obs (only if both > 0)

moe_ci.statistic: per pair mean of D (nats/token) with percentile CI under every scheme; PPL difference exp(l_FC) - exp(l_FR) reported separately with its own percentile CI

decision_rules.resolved_variance: V_corr pivot 95% CI lower bound > 0 AND common-effect null p < 0.05 (primary scheme)
decision_rules.reliable_within: median split-half Pearson (primary scheme) >= 0.5 AND exceeds the null median distribution at p < 0.05

setting_verdict.A: both datasets resolved AND reliable, AND cross-dataset Pearson upper 95% bound < sqrt(lam_WT2 lam_C4)
setting_verdict.B: neither dataset resolved AND neither reliable
setting_verdict.C: exactly one dataset resolved-and-reliable, the other neither (or settings within a family differ)
setting_verdict.D: any other pattern (e.g. resolved but unreliable, both reliable but cross-dataset agreement not distinguishable from the attenuated expectation)

decision_rules.note: dose levels are reported per k with the same rules; a family-level dose summary is descriptive

constraints: negative V_corr reported raw; zero only as a separately labelled constrained estimate
